input: Build a mobile app for my bakery that works fully offline, always shows live inventory from the shop server, ships in one week, and has every feature a big chain app has.

tasks.title: Read me first: assumptions and gaps
tasks.description:
This plan is a starting point and may still have gaps. Read the items below before relying on it.
The dates are suggestions meant to keep momentum. Moving one is normal, and overdue cards simply show in red.
Pacing assumed: about 10 hours a week, starting Mon 26 Oct (you did not say how much time you have). If you add your hours per week or a start date to the description and generate again, the dates will follow.
Deadline Sat 31 Oct: NOT met at 10 hours a week. The last card is due Fri 27 Nov, about 19 working days late. The dates below are honest, not squeezed. To hit it, these would have to be deferred or dropped: "Register developer accounts and start store submission", "Decision: Ship week-one release or extend scope", "Build and test a release candidate", "Add privacy policy and legal basics", "Set up error monitoring", "Add authentication if decided", "Build core inventory UI screens", "Build inventory sync layer", "Build local database schema and offline storage". Or add more hours a week.
checklist: Assumption, verify: The shop server already exists and exposes some form of API (REST or similar) that the app can call to read inventory How to check: Check your shop server documentation or ask your point-of-sale vendor what API endpoints are available

Assumption, verify: The app will be published on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store How to check: Confirm which platforms your customers use; App Store review alone typically takes 1-3 days and may exceed the one-week deadline

Assumption, verify: Offline-first means the app shows the last-synced inventory snapshot when offline, not a guaranteed real-time feed How to check: Confirm with yourself or stakeholders what behavior is acceptable when the device has no connection

Assumption, verify: A developer (or AI coding assistant) is available full-time to meet the one-week window How to check: Estimate your own available hours for the week and compare with the effort totals in this plan
Assumption, verify: No existing mobile codebase exists; this is a fresh project How to check: Check whether any prior app or prototype exists that could be reused
On "Verify shop server API capability": If neither is available, assumption: verify that the shop server vendor can enable API access.
On "Set up error monitoring": Choose an error monitoring service compatible with Expo (Assumption, verify: confirm a free tier exists for small apps by checking the vendor's current pricing page)
On "Add privacy policy and legal basics": Check with a professional for any regulatory requirements specific to your location and type of app.
On "Add privacy policy and legal basics": Check with a professional whether local food retail laws require any specific disclosures in the app

On "Register developer accounts and start store submission": Register for an Apple Developer account and a Google Play Developer account if not already done (Assumption, verify: confirm current registration fees on the official de…
For any price, rate or rule above: check the vendor or official source directly, or ask a professional for anything legal or financial.
tasks.notes:
NOT MENTIONED IN YOUR DESCRIPTION (often matters):
- Which specific features the app needs (the description only says 'every feature a big chain app has', which is undefined and likely unachievable in one week)
- Who the app's users are: bakery staff, customers, or both
- Authentication: does the app require login, and if so by whom
- Whether the shop server API requires an API key, OAuth, or other credentials
- How inventory conflicts are resolved when edits are made offline and the server has also changed

THINGS THIS PLAN CANNOT KNOW:
- Current App Store and Google Play review times and policies
- What API the specific shop server exposes (this varies by vendor)
- Current Expo and WatermelonDB pricing and free-tier limits
- Local laws or regulations that may apply to a customer-facing food retail app (for example allergen disclosure requirements)

POSSIBLE CONFLICTS TO CHECK:
- "Set up error monitoring" rests on an unchecked assumption but its first step is not a check.

tasks.title: Decisions needed: choices only you can make
tasks.description: These choices were not in your description, so they are yours to make. Each has a recommended default: accept it and move on, or swap it for your own.
checklist: Who uses this app: bakery staff managing inventory, customers ordering or browsing, or both? Options: Staff only / Customers only / Both staff and customers with separate views. Recommended default: Staff only for v1, to keep scope achievable in one week.

What does 'fully offline' mean in practice when inventory cannot be live? Options: Show last-synced snapshot with a clear 'last updated' timestamp / Block inventory view entirely when offline / Allow offline edits that sync when reconnected. Recommended default: Show last-synced snapshot with a clear timestamp, and allow offline edits that sync on reconnect.

Which features are in scope for the first release given the one-week constraint? Options: Inventory view and sync only / Inventory plus ordering / Full feature parity with a large chain app. Recommended default: Inventory view and sync only for week one; additional features in later sprints.

Will the app be distributed through the App Store and Google Play, or through a private/internal channel? Options: Public App Store and Google Play (review time risk) / TestFlight and internal track only (faster) / Side-loaded APK for Android only (no review). Recommended default: TestFlight and internal track for week one to avoid review delays.
Does the app need user login and accounts? Options: No login required / Simple PIN or password / Full account system with email/password. Recommended default: Simple PIN for staff-only v1.
Recommended default for mobile: React Native (Expo). Why: single codebase for iOS and Android, large beginner-friendly ecosystem, works well with offline-first libraries
Recommended default for local storage / offline sync: WatermelonDB. Why: designed for offline-first React Native apps with background sync
Recommended default for backend / shop server integration: REST or existing shop server API. Why: connect to whatever the shop server already exposes rather than rebuilding it
Recommended default for push notifications: Expo Notifications. Why: built into Expo, handles both platforms

tasks.title: Decision: Resolve conflicting requirements before building
tasks.description:
The stated goals conflict in two ways: a fully offline app cannot show live inventory, and one week cannot deliver every feature a large chain app has. Resolve both before writing any code.
Why this matters: Building without resolving these means rework or a product nobody can use.
checklist: Decide what offline inventory display means (last-synced snapshot, offline edits, or something else)
Write down the exact feature list for week one (not 'everything a chain app has')
Decide who uses the app and whether login is needed
Confirm distribution channel (public stores vs internal) and check review timelines
Record all decisions in a shared note so the whole team builds the same thing
tasks.notes: Offline-first: the device stores a copy of data locally and syncs with the server when a connection is available. This card must be finished before any other card starts.

tasks.title: Verify shop server API capability
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Resolve conflicting requirements before building
Confirm exactly what the shop server exposes before building the sync layer around it.
Why this matters: If the server has no API, the entire sync plan must change.
checklist: Verify the shop server exposes an API (check docs or ask the vendor)
List the available inventory endpoints and what data they return
Check authentication method required (API key, username/password, OAuth, or none)
Confirm whether the server supports push/webhook or only polling
Document the base URL, auth method, and key fields (item name, quantity, price) in a shared note
tasks.notes: Polling: the app asks the server for new data on a schedule. Webhook: the server pushes updates to the app automatically. If neither is available, assumption: verify that the shop server vendor can enable API access.

tasks.title: Set up development environment and project
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Resolve conflicting requirements before building
Create the Expo React Native project and configure the tools every other card depends on.
Why this matters: Nothing else can be built without a working project scaffold.
checklist: Install Node.js and the Expo CLI on the development machine
Run 'npx create-expo-app bakery-app' to create the project
Install WatermelonDB and configure it for React Native
Set up a Git repository and push the initial project
Confirm the app opens on a real device or emulator
tasks.notes: Expo CLI: a command-line tool that creates and manages React Native projects. Emulator: a program that mimics a phone on your computer.

tasks.title: Register developer accounts and start store submission
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Resolve conflicting requirements before building
Create Apple Developer and Google Play accounts and begin the submission process as early as possible given review times.
Why this matters: Store review can take days and will blow the one-week deadline if started late.
checklist: Check current Apple App Store and Google Play review times on their official developer pages
Register for an Apple Developer account and a Google Play Developer account if not already done (Assumption, verify: confirm current registration fees on the official developer portals)
Prepare store listing assets: app name, short description, screenshots
Submit the app to TestFlight (Apple) and the internal test track (Google) as soon as a working build exists
tasks.notes: TestFlight: Apple's platform for distributing test builds to users without going through the full App Store review. If the one-week deadline is firm, internal/test distribution is safer than waiting for public store review.

tasks.title: Build local database schema and offline storage
tasks.description:
Depends on: Set up development environment and project
Define the on-device database tables that store inventory data so the app works without a connection.
Why this matters: The offline inventory view and sync both depend on a working local database.
checklist: Define a WatermelonDB schema with at least an items table (name, quantity, price, last_synced_at)
Add a sync_metadata table to track the last successful sync time
Write a migration file so schema changes can be applied without data loss
Seed the database with a few sample items to support testing
Confirm data persists after the app is closed and reopened
tasks.notes: Schema: the structure (columns and types) of your database tables. Migration: a script that updates the database structure without deleting existing data.

tasks.title: Build inventory sync layer
tasks.description:
Depends on: Verify shop server API capability; Build local database schema and offline storage
Write the code that fetches inventory from the shop server and writes it to the local database, and that pushes any offline edits back when a connection is restored.
Why this matters: This is the bridge between the shop server and the offline-capable app.
checklist: Write a sync function that calls the shop server API and upserts items into the local database
Record last_synced_at after each successful sync
Implement a network listener that triggers sync automatically when the device comes back online
If offline edits are in scope (per earlier decision), queue local changes and push them on reconnect
Handle API errors gracefully and surface a clear message to the user
Test sync with the device in airplane mode, then reconnecting
tasks.notes: Upsert: insert a record if it does not exist, or update it if it does. Network listener: code that watches for the device's connection status to change.

tasks.title: Build core inventory UI screens
tasks.description:
Depends on: Build local database schema and offline storage
Create the screens that display inventory items from the local database and show sync status to the user.
Why this matters: This is the primary value the app delivers in week one.
checklist: Build an inventory list screen that reads from the local database
Show item name, quantity, and price per row
Display a 'Last synced: [time]' label prominently so the user knows the data age
Show an 'Offline' banner when the device has no connection
Add a manual refresh button that triggers a sync when online
Confirm the screen loads from local data with no network connection

tasks.title: Add authentication if decided
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Resolve conflicting requirements before building; Set up development environment and project
Implement whichever login method was chosen in the decisions card: none, PIN, or full accounts.
Why this matters: Prevents unauthorized access to inventory data.
checklist: Implement the authentication method chosen in the earlier decision (skip this card if no login is needed)
Gate the inventory screens behind the login flow
Store credentials securely using Expo SecureStore, not plain text
Test that closing and reopening the app does not bypass the login
tasks.notes: SecureStore: a device-level encrypted storage area provided by Expo for sensitive values like passwords or tokens.

tasks.title: Set up error monitoring
tasks.description:
Depends on: Set up development environment and project
Add basic crash and error logging so problems in production are visible without waiting for user reports.
Why this matters: Silent crashes make a small app look untrustworthy and are hard to debug later.
checklist: Choose an error monitoring service compatible with Expo (Assumption, verify: confirm a free tier exists for small apps by checking the vendor's current pricing page)
Install and configure the SDK in the project
Confirm a test error appears in the monitoring dashboard
tasks.notes: SDK: a small code library the monitoring service provides to send error reports from your app.

tasks.title: Add privacy policy and legal basics
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Resolve conflicting requirements before building
Create a minimal privacy policy and terms covering what data the app collects and stores.
Why this matters: App stores require a privacy policy, and food retail apps may have additional disclosure requirements.
checklist: List exactly what data the app collects (inventory snapshots, login credentials if any)
Check with a professional whether local food retail laws require any specific disclosures in the app
Draft a plain-language privacy policy and host it at a public URL
Add a link to the privacy policy in the app's settings or about screen
tasks.notes: Check with a professional for any regulatory requirements specific to your location and type of app.

tasks.title: Build and test a release candidate
tasks.description:
Depends on: Build inventory sync layer; Build core inventory UI screens; Add authentication if decided; Set up error monitoring; Add privacy policy and legal basics
Create a production build, run it on real devices, and fix any blockers before distribution.
Why this matters: A build that works in development may behave differently when packaged for release.
checklist: Run 'eas build' (Expo's cloud build service) to create a production APK and IPA
Install the build on at least one real Android device and one real iOS device
Test the full offline flow: open the app with no connection and confirm inventory is shown from local storage
Test the sync flow: go offline, make a change if offline edits are in scope, reconnect, confirm sync
Fix any crash or data loss bugs before distributing
tasks.notes: APK: the installable file format for Android apps. IPA: the installable file format for iOS apps. EAS: Expo Application Services, Expo's cloud build tool.

tasks.title: Decision: Ship week-one release or extend scope
tasks.description:
Depends on: Build and test a release candidate
Review what was built against what was decided in the first card and decide whether to ship or delay.
Why this matters: Shipping incomplete or broken software damages trust more than a short delay.
checklist: Confirm offline inventory display works on real devices
Confirm sync from shop server works when online
Confirm no data loss bugs are open
Confirm the agreed feature list from the first card is fully working
If all checks pass, distribute via TestFlight and internal track; otherwise record what is missing and set a new date
